summary: The host_flag fallback calls ComputeSNAGridLocal::compute_array(), which does not exist in that class and resolves to the empty Compute::compute_array(), so compute sna/grid/local/kk computes nothing at all on host-only KOKKOS builds.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:159-162 'if (host_flag) { ComputeSNAGridLocal::compute_array(); return; }'. ComputeSNAGridLocal declares only 'void compute_local() override;' (src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.h:32) and its base ComputeGridLocal declares 'void compute_local() override = 0;' (src/ML-SNAP/compute_grid_local.h:26); neither declares compute_array(), so the call binds to 'virtual void compute_array() {}' in src/compute.h:129. The sibling GPU-capable style calls the correct method (src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h host branch calls ComputeSNAGrid::compute_array(), which does exist).
failure_scenario: Any KOKKOS build without a GPU backend (LMPDeviceType == LMPHostType, so host_flag==1), or the /kk/host variant on a GPU build: 'compute c sna/grid/local/kk grid ...' + 'dump local' outputs the raw contents of the freshly malloc'd alocal array (uninitialized garbage, including the ix/iy/iz/x/y/z columns) instead of bispectrum components. No error is issued.
suggested_fix: Call ComputeSNAGridLocal::compute_local() in the host_flag branch.

summary: The ComputeNeigh kernel drops the compute-group filter, so every grid descriptor includes atoms outside the compute's group.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:438-452 and :458-487 loop 'for (int j = 0; j < ntotal; j++)' with no mask/groupbit test; the class never reads atom->mask (datamask_read = EMPTY_MASK at :54). The CPU original src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp:244-246 has 'if (!(mask[j] & groupbit)) continue;' inside the identical loop.
failure_scenario: 'group solute type 2' + 'compute g solute sna/grid/local/kk grid 10 10 10 ...' -> the /kk result includes all atoms of every type, so the bispectrum components differ from the CPU style for every grid point.
suggested_fix: Add TYPE_MASK|MASK_MASK to datamask_read, capture 'mask = atomKK->k_mask.view<DeviceType>()' in compute_local(), and skip j when '!(mask(j) & groupbit)' in both loops.

summary: k_cutsq is filled with cutsq[1][1] for every type pair, so multi-type systems use the type-1 cutoff for all neighbours instead of the per-type cutoff the CPU style uses.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:65-72: 'cutsq_tmp = cutsq[1][1]; for (i..ntypes) for (j..ntypes) { k_cutsq.view_host()(i,j) = k_cutsq.view_host()(j,i) = cutsq_tmp; ... }'. The base class builds a genuinely per-type table: src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp:80-88 'cut = 2.0*radelem[i]*rcutfac; cutsq[i][i] = cut*cut; ... cutsq[i][j] = cutsq[j][i] = cut*cut;'. The kernel then also queries the wrong element of that table: :446/:466 use 'rnd_cutsq(itype,jtype)' with itype hard-wired to 1 (:429), whereas the CPU uses 'cutsq[jtype][jtype]' (compute_sna_grid_local.cpp:255).
failure_scenario: Two atom types with different radelem (e.g. radelem 0.5 1.0): all neighbours are cut off at (2*radelem[1]*rcutfac)^2, so type-2 atoms that should be inside the cutoff are dropped (or spurious ones included) and the descriptors are wrong.
suggested_fix: Copy the real cutsq[i][j] table into k_cutsq and index it as rnd_cutsq(jtype,jtype) to match the CPU style.

summary: max_neighs is hard-coded to 100 while the ComputeNeigh kernel writes snaKK.rij/wj/rcutij/inside at an unbounded offset, so a grid point with more than 100 atoms inside the cutoff overruns the SNA neighbour arrays.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:176-177 '// max_neighs is defined here - think of more elaborate methods.  max_neighs = 100;' then :191 'snaKK.grow_rij(chunk_size, max_neighs, padding_factor);'. The kernel at :457-486 loops over all ntotal atoms and does 'snaKK.rij(ii,offset,0) = ...; ... offset++;' with no check against max_neighs. The CPU style sizes the arrays for the worst case: src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp:218 'snaptr->grow_rij(ntotal);'.
failure_scenario: A dense system or a large rcutfac where any grid point has >100 atoms within the cutoff: out-of-bounds device writes -> silent corruption of the SNA views or an illegal-memory-access abort.
suggested_fix: Compute the true maximum neighbour count per grid point (a first counting pass already exists at :438-452; reduce d_ninside to its max) and call grow_rij with that value, or bound offset by max_neighs and error out.

summary: The PreUi kernels look up 'type(iatom)' where iatom is a grid-point index, not an atom index, giving a wrong (or out-of-bounds) element for the central site.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:516-524, :529-536 and :541-549 all do 'int itype = type(iatom); int ielem = d_map[itype]; snaKK.pre_ui(iatom, j, ielem);' where iatom ranges over [0,chunk_size) grid points. The ComputeNeigh kernel in the same file states the correct convention at :429-431: 'const int itype = 1; int ielem = 0; if (chemflag) ielem = d_map[itype];', matching src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp:233-235. type() is also read unconditionally, while d_map is only filled when chemflag is set (:105-109, :117-119).
failure_scenario: Any run: for grid point ii the central element becomes map[type[ii]] instead of map[1]; with chemflag off d_map is uninitialized device memory, so pre_ui writes the self-term into a random element slot. When chunk_size > nlocal+nghost, type(iatom) is an out-of-bounds read.
suggested_fix: Replace the body with the ComputeNeigh convention: 'const int ielem = chemflag ? d_map[1] : 0;'.

summary: d_radelem/d_wjelem/d_sinnerelem/d_dinnerelem are allocated with 'nelements' entries but the constructor fills 'ntypes' of them, and sinner/dinner are written at index i instead of i-1, so any run with more atom types than SNAP elements writes past the end of the host mirrors.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:75-78 'MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_radelem,...,nelements); ... d_wjelem ... d_sinnerelem ... d_dinnerelem' (nelements defaults to 1, src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp:58) versus :95-102 'for (int i = 1; i <= atom->ntypes; i++) { h_radelem(i-1) = radelem[i]; h_wjelem(i-1) = wjelem[i]; if (switchinnerflag) { h_sinnerelem(i) = sinnerelem[i]; h_dinnerelem(i) = dinnerelem[i]; } }'. Note the inconsistent offset: radelem/wjelem use i-1 but sinnerelem/dinnerelem use i, so even with ntypes == nelements == 1 the sinner/dinner write is one past the end.
failure_scenario: 'compute c all sna/grid/local/kk grid ... switchinnerflag 1 sinner 1.0 dinner 0.5' with a single type: h_sinnerelem(1) is written into a length-1 view -> heap overflow; with 2 types and no chem keyword (nelements==1) radelem/wjelem overflow as well.
suggested_fix: Size the four views with atom->ntypes (or ntypes+1) and use a single consistent offset (i-1) for all four.

summary: setup() calls ComputeGridLocal::setup() (which memory->create()s alocal and sets gridlocal_allocated=1) and then overwrites the alocal pointer with a Kokkos allocation, leaking the first array and making the next setup()'s deallocate() call free() on the interior of a Kokkos view.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:143-152: 'ComputeGridLocal::setup(); memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_alocal, alocal, size_local_rows, size_local_cols, "grid:alocal"); array_local = alocal;'. src/ML-SNAP/compute_grid_local.cpp:70-77 setup() -> allocate(); allocate() at :108-115 does 'gridlocal_allocated = 1; memory->create(alocal, size_local_rows, size_local_cols, ...)'. deallocate() at :121-130 does 'if (gridlocal_allocated) { gridlocal_allocated = 0; memory->destroy(alocal); }', and Memory::destroy(TYPE **&array) at src/memory.h:208-214 performs 'sfree(array[0]); sfree(array);' - array[0] then points into the Kokkos View host data allocated by MemoryKokkos::create_kokkos (src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:200-217). Compare compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:145-150 which deliberately does NOT call ComputeGrid::setup() but only set_grid_global()/set_grid_local(). The same defect exists in src/KOKKOS/compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp:111.
failure_scenario: A second 'run' command (modify->setup() calls compute[i]->setup() every run, src/modify.cpp:301): deallocate() calls free() on a pointer into a Kokkos allocation -> heap corruption / abort. Even a single run leaks size_local_rows*size_local_cols doubles.
suggested_fix: Mirror compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h: call only ComputeGridLocal::set_grid_global()/set_grid_local(), then destroy the previous k_alocal before create_kokkos(); leave gridlocal_allocated at 0.

summary: Neighbour weights and cutoff radii are looked up by element index while the CPU style looks them up by atom type, so they differ whenever the type-to-element map is not the identity.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:467-475 'int jelem = 0; if (chemflag) jelem = d_map[jtype]; ... snaKK.wj(ii,offset) = d_wjelem[jelem]; snaKK.rcutij(ii,offset) = (2.0*d_radelem[jelem])*rcutfac;'. The CPU original uses the type: src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp:260-261 'snaptr->wj[ninside] = wjelem[jtype]; snaptr->rcutij[ninside] = 2.0 * radelem[jtype] * rcutfac;'. Combined with the i-1 shift at :96-97, even the identity case is off by one relative to the CPU indexing.
failure_scenario: 'chem 2 0 1 1' with three types: types 2 and 3 both map to element 1 and get element 1's weight/radius, while the CPU style gives each type its own wjelem/radelem -> different descriptors.
suggested_fix: Index d_wjelem/d_radelem by jtype (with the same offset used when filling them) as the CPU style does.

summary: compute_local() never sets invoked_local, unlike the CPU style and the sibling gaussian/grid/local/kk style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:156-172 has no 'invoked_local = update->ntimestep;'. The CPU original sets it first thing: src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp:205-207. The sibling KOKKOS style does too: src/KOKKOS/compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp:134.
failure_scenario: Callers that guard on invoked_local (src/library.cpp:2799 lammps_extract_compute, src/REACTION/fix_bond_react.cpp:2413) re-run the whole grid computation on every access in the same timestep.
suggested_fix: Add 'invoked_local = update->ntimestep;' at the top of compute_local().

summary: Leftover debug scaffolding: an <iostream> include (against the project rule banning C++ iostreams), an unused d_test view, and dead grid-coordinate code in the Fill kernel.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:38 '#include <iostream>'; :79-80 '// test\n MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_test, "ComputeSNAGridLocalKokkos::test", nelements);' with :91-92 and :120 filling/copying it, and d_test declared at compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos.h:250 but never read; :711-742 in TagCSNAGridLocal2Fill recompute ix/iy/iz and xgrid[] (including the triclinic transform) but never use them, since ComputeNeigh already wrote columns 0-5 at :419-424; :723 leaves a commented-out printf.
failure_scenario: No wrong numbers, but the iostream include violates the LAMMPS coding rule and the dead code costs a triclinic matrix-vector product per grid point.
suggested_fix: Delete the <iostream> include, the d_test view and its mirror, and the unused coordinate block in TagCSNAGridLocal2Fill.

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly); found by group 04
summary: The host_flag fallback of compute sna/grid/local/kk calls ComputeSNAGridLocal::compute_array(), a method that class does not define (it only has compute_local), so the call binds to the empty Compute::compute_array() and nothing is computed on host-only KOKKOS builds; compute gaussian/grid/local/kk simply returns in the same situation (line 130).
evidence: compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:159-160; compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp:130-132; host_flag = (execution_space == HostKK) is true for the plain /kk style on any CPU-only Kokkos build.
failure_scenario: CPU-only Kokkos build (or /kk/host): dump local of these computes writes uninitialized/zero descriptors with no error.
suggested_fix: Call ComputeSNAGridLocal::compute_local() / ComputeGaussianGridLocal::compute_local() in the host branch.

summary: pair gran/hooke/kk ignores fix rigid body masses when computing the effective mass meff, silently producing different damping forces than the CPU style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hooke_kokkos.cpp:280 'KK_FLOAT meff = imass*jmass / (imass+jmass);' uses only rmass[i]/rmass[j] (lines 211,243). The CPU base src/GRANULAR/pair_gran_hooke.cpp:111-120 does 'mi = rmass[i]; mj = rmass[j]; if (fix_rigid) { if (mass_rigid[i] > 0.0) mi = mass_rigid[i]; if (mass_rigid[j] > 0.0) mj = mass_rigid[j]; } meff = mi*mj/(mi+mj);' and pair_gran_hooke.cpp:19-33 refreshes/communicates mass_rigid every reneighboring. 'grep -n fix_rigid src/KOKKOS/pair_gran*' returns nothing, and PairGranHooke::init_style (via PairGranHookeHistory::init_style, src/GRANULAR/pair_gran_hooke_history.cpp:42-52) still sets fix_rigid without any /kk error check. doc/src/pair_gran.rst:201-203 documents the rigid-body mass substitution as part of the model.
failure_scenario: Granular input with 'fix rigid' (or rigid/small) plus 'pair_style gran/hooke/kk': the velocity-damping term meff*gamman*vnnr and the friction cap meff*gammat*vrel use the individual particle mass instead of the body mass -> different trajectories than the identical non-kk run, with no warning.
suggested_fix: Port the mass_rigid lookup (a device DualView filled from fix_rigid->extract plus a forward comm) into the Kokkos kernels, or at minimum error out in PairGranHooke*Kokkos::init_style when fix_rigid is non-null.

summary: gran/hooke/kk stores the special_bonds lj factors into the base class's int special_lj[4], truncating fractional factors to 0 or 1.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hooke_kokkos.cpp:125-128 'special_lj[0] = force->special_lj[0]; ...' with src/pair.h:247 'int special_lj[4];    // copied from force->special_lj for Kokkos' -- PairGranHookeKokkos declares no KK_FLOAT special_lj of its own (see src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hooke_kokkos.h:63-96), unlike e.g. src/KOKKOS/pair_gauss_cut_kokkos.h:89 'KK_FLOAT special_lj[4];'. The kernel then does src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hooke_kokkos.cpp:234 'KK_FLOAT factor_lj = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(special_lj[sbmask(j)]);' and line 237 'if (factor_lj == 0) continue;'. The CPU base uses the true doubles: src/GRANULAR/pair_gran_hooke.cpp:45 'double *special_lj = force->special_lj;'.
failure_scenario: Granular run with bonded particles and 'special_bonds lj 0.5 1.0 1.0': the CPU style scales the 1-2 granular contact force by 0.5, while gran/hooke/kk truncates 0.5 to 0 and skips those pairs entirely (factor_lj == 0 -> continue).
suggested_fix: Declare a 'KK_FLOAT special_lj[4];' member in the three KOKKOS granular pair style headers (shadowing Pair::special_lj as the other KOKKOS pair styles do), or change Pair::special_lj to double.

summary: All three KOKKOS granular pair styles (gran/hooke, gran/hooke/history, gran/hertz/history) compute the effective mass from rmass alone and never substitute the rigid-body mass, so combining them with fix rigid gives different damping and friction forces than the CPU styles, silently.
verified_by: orchestrator (src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hooke_kokkos.cpp:280 and pair_gran_{hooke,hertz}_history_kokkos.cpp:350 'meff = imass*jmass/(imass+jmass)'; the CPU base substitutes mass_rigid at src/GRANULAR/pair_gran_hooke.cpp:149-162 and refreshes/forward-communicates it at :66-73. grep for fix_rigid or mass_rigid over src/KOKKOS/pair_gran*.{cpp,h} returns nothing, and the /kk init_style adds no guard.)

summary: alpha_step() and the x0 snapshot treat xvec as a flat 3*nlocal alias of atom->x, which is only valid for LayoutRight; unlike every other loop in the min/kk styles these three kernels have no F_LAYOUTRIGHT branch, so a KOKKOS_LAYOUT=default GPU build moves the wrong coordinates.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/min_linesearch_kokkos.cpp:108-109 'if (nvec) xvec = DAT::t_kkfloat_1d(d_x.data(),nvec); if (nvec) fvec = DAT::t_kkacc_1d(d_f.data(),nvec);' aliases the (nmax,3) view k_x as a flat length-3*nlocal view.  The three loops that use it are unguarded: :252-254 'Kokkos::parallel_for(nvec, LAMMPS_LAMBDA(const int& i) { l_x0[i] = l_xvec[i]; });', :391-393 'l_xvec[i] = l_x0[i];' and :410-412 'l_xvec[i] += static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(alpha)*l_h[i];'.  Everywhere else the same file and its subclasses do branch, precisely because the flat alias is layout-dependent: min_kokkos.h:27 'static constexpr int F_LAYOUTRIGHT = std::is_same<LMPDeviceLayout,Kokkos::LayoutRight>::value;', min_linesearch_kokkos.cpp:191-204 and :286-304, min_cg_kokkos.cpp:68-86, :125-143 and :178-196, min_kokkos.cpp:624-636/661-673/698-711.  src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:177-185 defines LMPDeviceLayout as Kokkos::LayoutRight only for LMP_KOKKOS_LAYOUT_LEGACY; with '-D KOKKOS_LAYOUT=default' (cmake/Modules/Packages/KOKKOS.cmake:33-40) it becomes LMPDeviceType::array_layout, i.e. Kokkos::LayoutLeft on CUDA/HIP.  Under LayoutLeft the flat view of length 3*nlocal covers x(0..3*nlocal-1, 0) -- the x-components of the first 3*nlocal atoms including ghosts -- not (x,y,z) of the first nlocal atoms.
failure_scenario: cmake -D KOKKOS_LAYOUT=default with a CUDA/HIP backend and 'min_style cg/kk': the line search snapshots and restores only x-components (of owned and ghost atoms) and adds alpha*h into those slots, so y and z are never stepped and ghost x-coordinates are corrupted. The minimization silently converges to garbage; with LAYOUT=legacy (the default) the code is correct, which is why CI does not see it.
suggested_fix: Give these three loops the same 'if constexpr (F_LAYOUTRIGHT) ... else' treatment as the fvec loops, indexing atomKK->k_x.view_device()(i,0..2) with j = 3*i in the LayoutLeft branch; do the same for the xvec loops in min_quickmin_kokkos/min_fire_kokkos, or reject KOKKOS_LAYOUT=default in MinKokkos::init().

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly); found by group 05
summary: The x0 snapshot/restore and the alpha step treat xvec as a flat 3*nlocal alias of the (nmax,3) x view without the F_LAYOUTRIGHT branch that every other loop in the min/kk styles has, so with KOKKOS_LAYOUT=default on a GPU (LayoutLeft) the wrong coordinates are moved.
evidence: min_linesearch_kokkos.cpp:108 (flat alias), 253/392/411 unguarded xvec loops vs guarded loops at 191, 286, 442.
failure_scenario: cmake -D KOKKOS_LAYOUT=default + CUDA/HIP + min_style cg/kk: only x components (incl. ghosts) are stepped; y/z never move. Default legacy layout is unaffected.
suggested_fix: Add the LayoutLeft branch (index k_x.view_device()(i,0..2)) or reject KOKKOS_LAYOUT=default in MinKokkos::init().

summary: Special-bonds handling diverges from the CPU style: the KOKKOS kernel multiplies the whole damped DSF prefactor by factor_coul instead of subtracting (1-factor_coul)*prefactor, so excluded/scaled pairs get the wrong Coulomb force and energy.
evidence: src/pair_coul_dsf.cpp:108-114 'prefactor = qqrd2e * qtmp * q[j] / r; ... forcecoul = prefactor * (erfcc / r + 2.0 * alpha / MY_PIS * erfcd + r * f_shift) * r; if (factor_coul < 1.0) forcecoul -= (1.0 - factor_coul) * prefactor;' and :127-128 'ecoul = prefactor * (erfcc - r * e_shift - rsq * f_shift); if (factor_coul < 1.0) ecoul -= (1.0 - factor_coul) * prefactor;' (PairCoulDSF::single, src/pair_coul_dsf.cpp:295-299, uses the same convention).  src/KOKKOS/pair_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:260 'const KK_FLOAT prefactor = factor_coul * qqrd2e*qtmp*q[j]/r;' and :264-265/:281 compute forcecoul and ecoul from that prefactor with NO '(1-factor_coul)*prefactor' subtraction.  The correctly ported sibling src/KOKKOS/pair_born_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:212-213 and :261-262 does 'forcecoul -= (1.0-factor_coul)*prefactor;' / 'ecoul -= (1.0-factor_coul)*prefactor;'.
failure_scenario: Any molecular system run with pair_style coul/dsf/kk and special_bonds coul 0.0 0.0 0.0: for every 1-2/1-3/1-4 pair inside cut_coul the CPU adds prefactor*(X-1) (the DSF damping/shift remainder, X = erfcc + 2*alpha*r*erfcd/MY_PIS + r*r*f_shift) while the /kk style adds exactly 0, so forces and eng_coul differ from the CPU reference.
suggested_fix: Drop factor_coul from the prefactor and add 'if (factor_coul < 1.0) forcecoul -= (1.0-factor_coul)*prefactor;' / the same for ecoul, mirroring src/pair_coul_dsf.cpp:114 and :128 (src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:223,248 carries the identical defect against src/EXTRA-PAIR/pair_lj_cut_coul_dsf.cpp:137-143).

summary: special_coul is applied by folding factor_coul into the prefactor instead of subtracting (1-factor_coul)*prefactor from forcecoul/ecoul as the CPU style does. With the LAMMPS default special_bonds coul 0 0 0 the KOKKOS style contributes exactly zero for 1-2/1-3/1-4 pairs while the CPU style contributes -prefactor. Identical defect in pair_lj_cut_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:223 and :248.
verified_by: orchestrator (src/KOKKOS/pair_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:260-266 vs src/pair_coul_dsf.cpp:108-115; the correctly ported sibling is pair_born_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:205-215, which uses the CPU form).

summary: get_kinetic_energy() reads the per-type mass dual view on the device without calling atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>() first, so it can use a stale (or never-copied) device mass array.
failure_scenario: A 'mass' command (or a data-file read) between runs marks k_mass host-modified; if fix momentum/kk with 'rescale yes' is the first device consumer of the masses, the reduction uses the previous (or zero-filled) device copy, so ekin_old/ekin_new and hence the rescale factor are wrong -- silently, since factor just becomes 1.0 when both are 0.
suggested_fix: Add 'atomKK->k_mass.template sync<DeviceType>();' next to the TYPE_MASK sync in get_kinetic_energy(), matching src/KOKKOS/group_kokkos.h.

summary: fix momentum/kk computes the group mass on the device from atomKK->k_mass without syncing the DualView.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_momentum_kokkos.cpp:70-77 `atomKK->sync(execution_space, TYPE_MASK); ... typename AT::t_kkfloat_1d_randomread mass = atomKK->k_mass.view<DeviceType>(); ... update += static_cast<double>(mass(type(i)) * ...)`.  TYPE_MASK is synced but there is no mask bit for mass and no `atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>()` anywhere in the file (all four sync calls are lines 60,70,88,143).  k_mass is written host-side only, with `modify_host()` (src/KOKKOS/atom_kokkos.cpp:287-316).
failure_scenario: GPU run with per-type masses and no other style having synced k_mass: the group mass sums to zero, so `fix momentum` divides by zero when forming the centre-of-mass velocity (vcm = p/masstotal), producing NaN velocities for the whole group.
suggested_fix: Add `atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();` (the idiom used by FixNVEKokkos::init(), src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46) before the device view is used.

summary: The MEAM pair scale factor is stored in an INTEGER Kokkos view, so every non-integral 'fix adapt ... pair meam scale' value is truncated (0.5 becomes 0, 1.9 becomes 1) before it reaches the device kernels.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/meam_kokkos.h:65 'typename AT::t_int_2d d_scale;' and src/KOKKOS/pair_meam_kokkos.h:108 'typename AT::t_int_2d d_scale;'. It is filled from the CPU double array by an implicit narrowing conversion at src/KOKKOS/pair_meam_kokkos.cpp:303-307: 'for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) { h_map[i] = map[i]; for (int j = 1; j <= n; j++) h_scale(i,j) = scale[i][j]; }' where PairMEAM::scale is 'double **' (src/MEAM/pair_meam.cpp:170 'memory->create(scale, np1, np1, "pair:scale");'). It is then read as a floating-point factor: src/KOKKOS/meam_dens_final_kokkos.h:63 'scaleii = d_scale(type[i],type[i]);' followed by ':182 Fl *= scaleii;', and src/KOKKOS/meam_force_kokkos.h:186-187 'KK_FLOAT scaleij = d_scale(type[i], type[i]);'. 'scale' is a documented fix adapt target for pair meam (doc/src/fix_adapt.rst:243: '| :doc:`meam <pair_meam>` | scale | type pairs |'), and PairMEAM::extract exposes it (src/MEAM/pair_meam.cpp:895-898 'if (strcmp(str, "scale") == 0) return (void *) scale;').
failure_scenario: 'pair_style meam/kk ...' plus 'fix adapt 1 pair meam scale 1 1 v_ramp' with v_ramp going 1.0 -> 0.0: the CPU style scales the MEAM energy smoothly, while the /kk style sees d_scale = 1 until the value drops below 1.0 and then 0, so the embedding energy of every atom of that type jumps discontinuously to zero. Any fractional scale (the normal case for a thermodynamic-integration ramp) is silently wrong.
suggested_fix: Declare d_scale as a floating-point view ('typename AT::t_kkfloat_2d') in both src/KOKKOS/meam_kokkos.h:65 and src/KOKKOS/pair_meam_kokkos.h:108 (and in the meam_dens_final signature at meam_dens_final_kokkos.h:25 / meam_kokkos.h:89), and re-copy scale[][] to the device whenever fix adapt can have changed it, not only in coeff().

summary: The reduction functor stores a raw host pointer to the RegBlockKokkos/RegSphereKokkos object and dereferences it inside the device kernel, which is an illegal memory access on CUDA/HIP unless the build opts into unified memory.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_region_kokkos.h:96-112 'FixWallRegionKokkos<DeviceType> c; T *regionKK; ... KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION void operator()(const int i, value_type result) const { c.wall_particle(regionKK,i,result); }' -- the fix itself is copied BY VALUE ('c(*c_ptr)') but the region is kept as a pointer, filled in src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_region_kokkos.cpp:117-122 with the address returned by 'dynamic_cast<RegBlockKokkos<DeviceType>*>(region)', i.e. an ordinary host-heap object created by Domain's region factory. The kernel then does 'regionKK->match_kokkos(...)' (fix_wall_region_kokkos.cpp:159) and 'regionKK->surface_kokkos(...)' (line 173), which read instance members such as dynamic/openflag/interior/xlo/xhi and the RegionRemapKokkos boxremap (src/KOKKOS/region_block_kokkos.h:68-119, 122-127) from that host address. Every other Kokkos style that needs a region avoids this by calling the region's own match_all_kokkos(), which copies '*this' into the kernel (e.g. src/KOKKOS/fix_setforce_kokkos.cpp:85-90, fix_addforce_kokkos.cpp:105-110, compute_temp_region_kokkos.cpp:69-70). UVM is not on by default: cmake/Modules/Packages/KOKKOS.cmake:58-64 rejects Kokkos_ENABLE_CUDA_UVM and doc/src/Speed_kokkos.rst:439-441 documents Kokkos_ENABLE_IMPL_CUDA_UNIFIED_MEMORY as an opt-in CMake option.
failure_scenario: 'region r block ... ' + 'fix w all wall/region/kk r lj93 1.0 1.0 2.5' on a CUDA or HIP build without Kokkos_ENABLE_IMPL_CUDA_UNIFIED_MEMORY: the first post_force kernel dereferences a host address on the device and the run dies with 'an illegal memory address was encountered' (or, worse, silently reads garbage region geometry and produces wrong wall forces).
suggested_fix: Pass the region object by value into the functor (store 'T regionKK;' copy-constructed from '*regionKK', the way the fix itself is copied) after setting the region's copymode, or restructure so the kernel is launched from inside the region class like match_all_kokkos() does.

summary: The fused ters_bij_k_and_ters_dbij() (the only bij derivative actually used by tersoff/kk) still contains the pre-2022 buggy extra 0.5 factor in the second term, so the bond-order prefactor differs from the CPU style and from the file's own unfused ters_dbij().
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_kokkos.cpp:836-838 `prefactor = param.beta * (factor * (1.0 - 0.5*(1.0 + 0.5/(prm_ijk_pn)) * tmp_pow_neg_prm_ijk_pn));` versus the corrected unfused version in the same file, lines 802-807: `return param.beta * (factor * /* error in negligible 2nd term fixed 2/21/2022 */ /* (1.0 - 0.5*(1.0 + 1.0/(2.0*param.powern)) * */ (1.0 - (1.0 + 0.5/(param.powern)) * Kokkos::pow(tmp,-param.powern)));` and the CPU base src/MANYBODY/pair_tersoff.cpp ters_bij_d(): `return param->beta * (-0.5*pow(tmp,-1.5) * (1.0 - (1.0 + 1.0/(2.0*param->powern)) * pow(tmp,-param->powern)));`. Line 436 `ters_bij_k_and_ters_dbij(d_params(iparam_ij),bo_ij,bij,prefactor);` is the call site; ters_dbij()/ters_bij_k() are dead code in this file. The sibling KOKKOS styles use the correct unfused form (pair_tersoff_zbl_kokkos.cpp:484, pair_tersoff_mod_kokkos.cpp:441, pair_tersoff_mod_c_kokkos.cpp:446).
failure_scenario: Any tersoff/kk configuration where beta*zeta falls in the (c2, c1] branch (roughly 2*n*1e-16 < (beta*zeta)^-n < 2*n*1e-8) gets a three-body prefactor that is wrong by ~half of the correction term (~1e-8 relative), so tersoff/kk forces do not match pair_style tersoff bit-for-bit in that branch.
suggested_fix: Drop the extra `0.5*` so the fused branch reads `(1.0 - (1.0 + 0.5/prm_ijk_pn) * tmp_pow_neg_prm_ijk_pn)`, matching ters_dbij() and the CPU base.

summary: Dead device helpers left behind after the fusing rewrite: ters_bij_k, ters_dbij, ters_fa_k, ters_dfa, ters_dthbj, ters_dthbk and v_tally3_atom are never called.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_kokkos.cpp defines ters_bij_k (780), ters_dbij (797), ters_fa_k (737), ters_dfa (749), ters_dthbj (938), ters_dthbk (1001), v_tally3_atom (1162); grep for call sites in the file yields only the fused `ters_fa_k_and_ters_dfa` (435), `ters_bij_k_and_ters_dbij` (436) and `ters_fc_k_and_ters_dfc` (507). They are exactly the copies that drifted out of sync with the fused versions (see the ters_dbij finding).
failure_scenario: No runtime effect, but the duplicated formulas are what let the fused/unfused divergence go unnoticed.
suggested_fix: Delete the unused helpers (or make the fused versions call them) so there is a single copy of each formula.

summary: The extent check in the TransposeHelperKokkos constructor compares the destination's second extent with itself instead of with the source, so a mismatched extent(1) is never caught.
evidence: transpose_helper_kokkos.h:78: 'assert(d_dst.extent(0) == d_src.extent(0) && d_dst.extent(1) == d_dst.extent(1));' -- the second operand is trivially true; intended is 'd_dst.extent(1) == d_src.extent(1)'.
failure_scenario: A caller passing views whose second extents differ (e.g. after a maxneighs change on only one of them) is not caught in debug builds; the transpose then reads or writes out of bounds instead of asserting. No effect on release builds (assert compiled out).
suggested_fix: Change the second comparison to d_src.extent(1).

summary: Twelve headers in src/KOKKOS have no include guard at all, and four more use guard macros without the project's LMP_ prefix.
evidence:
No #ifndef/#define guard anywhere in the file (progress_rules_D/rule6b.py -> rule6_guards.json):
  src/KOKKOS/transpose_helper_kokkos.h  (opens namespace LAMMPS_NS at line 21 right after #include "kokkos_type.h" on line 19)
  src/KOKKOS/pack_kokkos.h
  src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h
  src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h
  src/KOKKOS/pair_snap_kokkos_impl.h
  src/KOKKOS/sna_kokkos_impl.h
  src/KOKKOS/meam_dens_final_kokkos.h
  src/KOKKOS/meam_dens_init_kokkos.h
  src/KOKKOS/meam_force_kokkos.h
  src/KOKKOS/meam_funcs_kokkos.h
  src/KOKKOS/meam_impl_kokkos.h
  src/KOKKOS/meam_setup_done_kokkos.h
Non-LMP_-prefixed guards: src/KOKKOS/kokkos.h:15 KOKKOS_LMP_H, src/KOKKOS/kokkos_base.h:15 KOKKOS_BASE_H, src/KOKKOS/kokkos_few.h:2 KOKKOS_FEW_H, src/KOKKOS/rand_pool_wrap_kokkos.h:15 RAND_POOL_WRAP_H -- the KOKKOS_* ones sit in the macro namespace the Kokkos library itself uses.
Each unguarded file currently has exactly one includer (transpose_helper_kokkos.h <- npair_kokkos.cpp:25; pack_kokkos.h <- remap_kokkos.cpp:20; the *_impl.h and meam_*_kokkos.h files <- sna_kokkos.h / pair_snap_kokkos.cpp / compute_sna_grid*_kokkos.cpp / meam_impl_kokkos.h, itself reached only from the guarded meam_kokkos.h:275), so nothing breaks today.
failure_scenario: A second style that also needs the transpose helper (or a new .cpp that includes both meam_kokkos.h and one of the meam_*_kokkos.h pieces directly) produces 'redefinition of struct TransposeHelperKokkos' / duplicate template definitions, an error that only appears once the header gains a second user.
suggested_fix: Add the standard LMP_<FILENAME>_H #ifndef/#define/#endif guard to the twelve unguarded headers, and rename the four KOKKOS_*/RAND_POOL_WRAP_H guards to the LMP_ prefixed form.

summary: All UF3 spline coefficient/knot views are hardcoded to LMPDeviceType instead of the class's DeviceType template parameter, yet they are read from KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION kernels that are instantiated for LMPHostType as well (uf3/kk/host).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_uf3_kokkos.h:88-108 declares e.g. `Kokkos::View<KK_FLOAT **, LMPDeviceLayout, LMPDeviceType> d_coefficients_2b;`, `Kokkos::View<int **, LMPDeviceLayout, LMPDeviceType> map2b;`, `Kokkos::View<KK_FLOAT **[16], LMPDeviceLayout, LMPDeviceType> constants_2b;` (and 10 more). These are read in the device kernels: src/KOKKOS/pair_uf3_kokkos.cpp:560 `int interaction_id = map2b(itype, jtype);` and 562/573 inside `twobody()`, and 619/636/647 inside `threebody()`, which run under `Kokkos::RangePolicy<DeviceType,...>` (lines 796/800). src/KOKKOS/pair_uf3_kokkos.cpp:1664-1666 explicitly instantiates `PairUF3Kokkos<LMPHostType>` under LMP_KOKKOS_GPU. This is the same defect class the KOKKOS rules describe for `DAT::` per-atom views (.github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 3).
failure_scenario: On a CUDA/HIP build, `pair_style uf3/kk/host` (or `-k on ... -sf kk` with the host back end selected) runs the kernels on the host while these views live in device memory: Kokkos' memory-space access check aborts at the first `map2b(itype,jtype)`. On a CPU-only build both spaces coincide, so the defect is invisible.
suggested_fix: Change the memory space of these views (and d_cut_3b_list) from LMPDeviceType to the class template parameter DeviceType, as the neighbor-short views at lines 179-180 already do.

summary: The pass that measures the maximum bin occupancy increments k_bincount without zeroing it first, so it counts the previous neighbor build's occupancy on top of the current one and over-allocates the bins array by about a factor of two.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/nbin_ssa_kokkos.cpp:142-148 'atoms_per_bin = 0; copymode = 1; NPairSSAKokkosBinIDAtomsFunctor<DeviceType> f(*this); Kokkos::parallel_reduce(nlocal, f, atoms_per_bin);' and the kernel at :279-280 'const int ac = Kokkos::atomic_fetch_add(&(bincount[ibin]), (int)1); if (update <= ac) update = ac + 1;'.  Nothing zeroes bincount before this: bin_atoms_setup() (:61-91) only reallocates k_bincount when mbins grows past k_bins.view_host().extent(0) (:63-69), and the only zeroing is the MemsetZeroFunctor at :205-207, which runs AFTER the reduce, right before the real binning pass at :212-215.  bincount is therefore left holding the previous build's final per-bin counts.  Contrast the ghost counting pass at :157-166, which does zero its counter first ('for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) k_gbincount.view_host()(i) = 0; k_gbincount.modify_host(); k_gbincount.sync<DeviceType>();').  The CPU sibling src/DPD-REACT/nbin_ssa.cpp:63-65 likewise clears binhead[] before every build.
failure_scenario: Any run using neigh_modify binsize / pair_style dpd with nbin ssa/kk: from the second neighbor build on, atoms_per_bin reported by the reduce is about 2*max_bin_occupancy, and src/KOKKOS/nbin_ssa_kokkos.cpp:200-204 allocates k_bins as (mbins, atoms_per_bin), i.e. roughly double the memory it needs. Results stay correct because binAtomsItem() re-counts from a zeroed bincount.
suggested_fix: Run the MemsetZeroFunctor (or Kokkos::deep_copy(bincount,0)) on k_bincount before the binIDAtomsItem reduce as well, mirroring the k_gbincount reset used for the ghost pass.

summary: setup_tables() unconditionally copies tb->de, tb->df (and tb->f when NOF is used) into device views, but DihedralTable::compute_table() only fills those arrays for tabstyle LINEAR, so for tabstyle spline the copy reads uninitialized heap memory.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/dihedral_table_kokkos.cpp:372-379 `for (int i = 0; i < tablength; i++) { k_e.view_host()(m,i)=...; k_de.view_host()(m,i) = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(tb->de[i]); k_f_tab.view_host()(m,i) = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(tb->f[i]); k_df.view_host()(m,i) = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(tb->df[i]); ... }`.  src/MOLECULE/dihedral_table.cpp:1113-1119 allocates phi/e/de/f/df/e2/f2 with memory->create (uninitialized), and only the `else if (tabstyle == LINEAR)` branch at :1131-1164 fills de[] and df[]; the SPLINE branch at :1121-1130 fills only e[] (and f[] when !f_unspecified).
failure_scenario: dihedral_style table/kk spline N with a table file: setup_tables reads tablength*ntables uninitialized doubles per table (de, df, and f under NOF). Harmless in the kernel (the spline branch never reads d_de/d_df), but it is an uninitialized read that valgrind/MSan flags, and the double->float narrowing of garbage values is undefined behaviour in a KOKKOS single-precision build.
suggested_fix: Only copy de/df when tabstyle == LINEAR (and f when !tb->f_unspecified), or zero-initialize those arrays in DihedralTable::compute_table().

summary: Commented-out code left in compute_fpair().
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_buck6d_coul_gauss_dsf_kokkos.cpp:192 '    // ebuck6d *= sme;  // not needed for force path'
failure_scenario: none (cosmetic); LAMMPS review rules require removal of commented-out code
suggested_fix: Delete the commented-out statement.

summary: Unterminated reStructuredText emphasis on the kspace_style style list: '*pppm/tip4p/kk' is missing its closing asterisk, so the KOKKOS variant is not rendered as a style name.
evidence:
doc/src/kspace_style.rst:53 (excerpt):
  ... or *pppm/disp/tip4p/omp* or *pppm/tip4p/kk or *pppm/tip4p/omp* or *pppm/dielectic* ...
Every other entry on that line is delimited by a pair of asterisks; here the closing '*' after 'pppm/tip4p/kk' is missing, so Sphinx pairs the opening '*' of '*pppm/tip4p/kk' with the opening '*' of '*pppm/tip4p/omp*' and emphasises the text 'pppm/tip4p/kk or ' instead.  The style itself is real: src/KOKKOS/pppm_tip4p_kokkos.h registers KSpaceStyle(pppm/tip4p/kk,...) and doc/src/kspace_style.rst:28 has '.. index:: kspace_style pppm/tip4p/kk'.  (The same line also has an unmarked 'ewald/gpu' and a 'pppm/dielectic' typo for 'pppm/dielectric'.)
failure_scenario: The rendered kspace_style page shows a mangled style list around pppm/tip4p/kk, so a user searching the page for the KOKKOS TIP4P PPPM variant does not find it formatted like the other styles.
suggested_fix: Close the emphasis: '*pppm/tip4p/kk*'; while there, fix 'ewald/gpu' -> '*ewald/gpu*' and 'pppm/dielectic' -> '*pppm/dielectric*'.
